source_text:
Ὁ Χριστὸς δέ, καθὰ
ἔφημεν, ὡς νομοθέτης τὸν ἑαυτοῦ νόμον ὑπὲρ νόμον ἐπλήρωσεν· οὐδὲ γὰρ ἤνοιξεν,
ἀλλὰ κεκλεισμένην τὴν πύλην τῆς παρθένου κατέλιπεν, οὐκ ἐσύλησε τὴν σφραγῖδα
τῆς φύσεως, οὐκ ἐζη μίωσε τὴν τεκοῦσαν· ἀκέραιον γὰρ αὐτῇ τὸ σχῆμα τῆς παρθε
νίας κατέλιπεν. Εἰ δὲ ἀπιστεῖς, παρὰ τοῦ Ἰεζεκιὴλ μάνθανε· «Καὶ ἀπέστρεψέ με κατὰ
τὴν ὁδὸν τῆς πύλης τῶν ἁγίων τῆς ἐξω τέρας, τῆς βλεπούσης κατὰ ἀνατολάς, καὶ
αὕτη ἦν κεκλεισμένη. Καὶ εἶπε κύριος πρός με· Ἡ πύλη αὕτη κεκλεισμένη ἔσται, οὐκ
ἀνοιχθήσεται, καὶ οὐδεὶς οὐ μὴ διέλθῃ δι' αὐτῆς, ὅτι κύριος ὁ θεὸς τοῦ Ἰσραὴλ καὶ
εἰσελεύσεται καὶ ἐξελεύσεται, καὶ ἔσται κεκλεισμένη.» «Πᾶν ἄρσεν διανοῖγον
μήτραν ἅγιον τῷ κυ ρίῳ κληθήσεται.» Οὗτος δὲ οὐ μόνον ἅγιος. Ὅσον τοίνυν
ὑπερέχει τῷ ἁγιασμῷ, τοσοῦτον καὶ τῷ τόκῳ πλεονεκτεῖ καὶ τοῦ νόμου τὴν ἐντολὴν
ἀναβέβηκεν. Πλὴν δὲ ὅμως «τοῦ δοῦναι θυσίαν, κατὰ τὸ εἰρημένον ἐν νόμῳ κυρίου,
ζεῦγος τρυγόνων ἢ δύο νεοσσοὺς περιστερῶν.» Ἀτελῆ τὸν νόμον ὁ Λουκᾶς οὐκ
ἀγνοίᾳ κρατηθείς, σοφίᾳ δὲ ὁδηγηθεὶς ἐξέθετο. Ὁ μὲν νό μος ἔλεγεν· «ἀμνὸν καὶ
νεοσσόν»· οὐκ εὐποροῦντος δὲ τοῦ προσφέροντος, «ζεῦγος τρυγόνων ἢ δύο
νεοσσοὺς περιστερῶν καὶ σεμίδαλιν» προσέταττεν. Ὁ Λουκᾶς δὲ τὴν τοῦ πλουτοῦν
τος ἀφῆκεν προσφοράν· πτωχοῦ γὰρ ἐμνημόνευσε τοῦ δι' ἡμᾶς ἑκουσίως
πτωχεύσαντος. Οὐκ ἦν αὐτῷ, φησίν, κατάλυμα· πόθεν ἀμνὸν ἐκέκτητο; Ἐπὶ φάτνης
σπαργανωθείς, πόθεν προσέφερε πρόβατον; Μᾶλλον δὲ οὐκ ἔχρῃζεν ἀμνοῦ· αὐτὸς
γὰρ ἦν «ὁ ἀμνὸς τοῦ θεοῦ», τὸ ἀληθινὸν πρόβατον. Αὐτὸς ἑαυ τὸν ὑπὲρ τοῦ κόσμου
ἔθυεν· διὰ τοῦτο τί μὲν ὁ νόμος προσέταττεν ἐξηγόρευσεν, τί δὲ ὁ Χριστὸς οἰκονομεῖ
ἐσήμανεν.
4 Εἶτα ἑξῆς· «Καὶ ἰδοὺ ἄνθρωπος», φησίν, «ἐν Ἰερουσαλήμ, ᾧ ὄνομα Συμεών,
καὶ ὁ ἄνθρωπος οὗτος δίκαιος καὶ εὐλαβής, προσδεχόμενος παράκλησιν τῷ Ἰσραήλ,
καὶ Πνεῦμα ἅγιον ἦν ἐπ' αὐτῷ· καὶ ἦν αὐτῷ κεχρηματισμένον ὑπὸ τοῦ Πνεύματος
τοῦ ἁγίου μὴ ἰδεῖν θάνατον, πρὶν ἂν ἴδῃ τὸν Χριστὸν κυρίου.» Πολὺς ὁ τοῦ Συμεὼν
πλοῦτος, ποικίλα τοῦ στρατηγοῦ τὰ ὅπλα, γέμει καρπῶν τὸ φυτόν, γέμει βοτρύων ἡ
ἄμπελος. Οὐ μόνον «ἦν ἄνθρωπος», ἀλλὰ καὶ «Συμεὼν ὠνομάζετο». Πρὸς τούτοις
«δί καιος» οὐ μόνον «δίκαιος», ἀλλὰ καὶ «εὐλαβής», ἀλλὰ καὶ πα ράκλησιν ἐζήτει
τῷ Ἰσραήλ, ἀλλὰ καὶ «Πνεῦμα ἅγιον ἦν ἐπ' αὐ τῷ», ἀλλὰ καὶ «χρηματισθεὶς ὑπῆρχεν
μὴ ἰδεῖν θάνατον πρὶν ἂν ἴδῃ τὸν Χριστὸν κυρίου.» «Ἰδοὺ ἄνθρωπος»· ποῦ; «Ἐν
Ἰερουσαλήμ». Ἔκπληξιν ἡ λέξις ἔχει, γέμει τὸ ῥῆμα θαύματος· ἐν Ἰερουσαλὴμ
ἄνθρωπος περὶ ἧς Σοφονίας ὁ προφήτης τὸν θεὸν αὐτὸν εἰσήγαγε λέγοντα·
«Ἐξερευνήσω τὴν Ἰερουσαλὴμ μετὰ λύχνου καὶ οὐ μὴ εὕρω.» Καὶ λύχνου χρῄζει τὸ
φῶς; Οὔ φησιν, ἀλλὰ λύχνον καλεῖ τὸν νόμον. «Καὶ ἰδοὺ ἄν θρωπος ἐν Ἰερουσαλὴμ
ᾧ ὄνομα Συμεών.» Καὶ τίς ἡ ἑρμηνεία τοῦ δηλωθέντος ὀνόματος; «Ἀκοὴ θεοῦ», ὥστε
πρέπουσαν τῇ πολιτείᾳ τὴν προσηγορίαν ἐκ τῆς τοῦ πνεύματος οἰκονομίας ἐ
κτήσατο· ὅπου γὰρ «ἀκοὴ θεοῦ», ἐκεῖ πάντως ὑπακοὴ νόμου, τήρησις ἐντολῶν,
ἀγαθοῦ βίου δρόμος, σκοπὸς σωτηρίας εἰς τέ λος προσερχόμενος· ἐν οἷς ὁ ἀληθινὸς
χαρακτηρίζεται ἄνθρω πος, περὶ οὗ ταῦτα κατὰ λόγον ἐπήγαγεν.
5 «Καὶ ὁ ἄνθρωπος οὗτος δίκαιος καὶ εὐλαβής, προσδεχό μενος παράκλησιν
τοῦ Ἰσραήλ»· τοῦτο δικαίου σκοπὸς μὴ ζητεῖν τὸ ἑαυτοῦ, ἀλλὰ τὸ τοῦ ἑτέρου καὶ τῶν
πολλῶν, τῆς κοι νῆς σωτηρίας μὴ τῆς ἰδίας ἀπολαύσεως γίνεσθαι. «Καὶ Πνεῦμα»,
φησίν, «ἅγιον ἦν ἐπ' αὐτῷ»· ὄχημα ὑπῆρχε δεσποτικὸν ὁ Συμεών, θρόνος θεοῦ, καὶ
διὰ τοῦτο μετὰ χεῖρας τὸν βασιλέα τῶν αἰώνων ἐδέξατο.
thought_title: Christ fulfills the law without opening the virgin's womb; Simeon's wealth of virtues
orientation: Hesychius is expounding Luke's account of the Presentation, arguing that Christ as lawgiver fulfilled the law without violating Mary's virginity, and then begins to praise Simeon's righteousness.
pass_a_gloss: But Christ, as we said, as lawgiver fulfilled his own law above the law; for he did not open, but left the gate of the virgin (her physical virginity) closed, he did not despoil the seal of nature, he did not defile the one who bore him; for he left intact for her the form of virginity. But if you disbelieve, learn from Ezekiel: 'And he turned me back along the way of the gate of the holy places, the outer one, the one looking toward the east, and it was closed. And the Lord said to me: This gate shall be closed, it shall not be opened, and no one shall ever pass through it, because the Lord, the God of Israel, will enter and will go out, and it shall be closed.' 'Every male opening the womb shall be called holy to the Lord.' But this one is not only holy. As much therefore as he excels in sanctification, so much also does he have the advantage in birth and has gone beyond the commandment of the law. But nevertheless 'to give a sacrifice, according to what is said in the law of the Lord, a pair of turtledoves or two young pigeons.' Luke set forth the law as incomplete, not seized by ignorance but guided by wisdom. The law said: 'a lamb and a young pigeon'; but when the one offering was not well supplied, it commanded 'a pair of turtledoves or two young pigeons and fine flour.' But Luke left aside the offering of the rich man; for he mentioned the poor man who for our sake willingly became poor. There was no lodging for him, it says; from where had he acquired a lamb? Wrapped in swaddling clothes in a manger, from where did he offer a sheep? But rather he did not need a lamb; for he himself was 'the lamb of God,' the true sheep. He himself was sacrificing himself for the world; for this reason he declared what the law commanded, and signified what Christ was arranging. Then next: 'And behold a man,' it says, 'in Jerusalem, whose name was Simeon, and this man was righteous and devout, awaiting consolation for Israel, and the Holy Spirit was upon him; and it had been revealed to him by the Holy Spirit that he would not see death before he saw the Christ of the Lord.' Great is the wealth of Simeon, varied are the weapons of the general, Simeon is a plant full of fruits, a vine full of grape clusters. Not only 'was a man,' but also 'was named Simeon.' In addition to these things 'righteous,' not only 'righteous,' but also 'devout,' but also he sought consolation for Israel, but also 'the Holy Spirit was upon him,' but also 'he had been warned not to see death before he saw the Christ of the Lord.' 'Behold a man'; where? 'In Jerusalem.' The word has astonishment, the saying is full of wonder; in Jerusalem a man, about which Zephaniah the prophet introduced God himself saying: 'I will search Jerusalem with a lamp and I will not find.' And does the light need a lamp? No, it says, but he calls the law a lamp. 'And behold a man in Jerusalem whose name was Simeon.' And what is the interpretation of the name that was indicated? 'Hearing of God,' so that he acquired a name befitting his way of life from the dispensation of the Spirit; for where there is 'hearing of God,' there is altogether obedience to the law, keeping of commandments, course of a good life, goal of salvation coming to the end; in these things the true man is characterized, about whom he brought these things forward according to reason. 'And this man was righteous and devout, awaiting consolation of Israel'; this is the goal of a righteous man, not to seek his own things, but the things of the other and of the many, to become of the common salvation, not of private enjoyment. 'And the Holy Spirit,' it says, 'was upon him'; Simeon was a vehicle of the Lord, a throne of God, and for this reason he received with his hands the king of the ages.

choices.english: fulfilled his own law above the law
choices.why: Keeps the paradox that Christ as lawgiver goes beyond the law's requirement while still fulfilling it; 'above the law' preserves the prepositional force.
rejected: fulfilled the law beyond the law

choices.why: Literal rendering preserves the Ezekiel gate imagery that Hesychius immediately develops; 'womb' would lose the typological link.

choices.term: ἀκέραιον αὐτῇ τὸ σχῆμα τῆς παρθενίας κατέλιπεν
choices.english: he left intact for her the form of virginity
choices.why: 'Form' keeps σχῆμα's sense of outward condition or state; 'intact' renders ἀκέραιον as undamaged.

choices.term: Ἀτελῆ τὸν νόμον ὁ Λουκᾶς οὐκ ἀγνοίᾳ κρατηθείς, σοφίᾳ δὲ ὁδηγηθεὶς ἐξέθετο
choices.english: Luke set forth the law as incomplete, not seized by ignorance but guided by wisdom
choices.why: Preserves the contrast between ignorance and wisdom and the sense that Luke deliberately presented the law's provision as partial.
rejected: Luke set forth the imperfect law
Luke expounded the law as deficient

choices.why: Direct biblical allusion to John 1:29; kept literal as the standard English form.
Literal rendering of the etymology Hesychius gives for Simeon's name; preserves the wordplay with obedience (ὑπακοή) that follows.

pass_b_english: But Christ, as we have said, fulfilled his own law as lawgiver above the law. For he did not open the gate of the virgin, but left it closed. He did not break the seal of nature, nor did he harm the one who bore him; he left intact for her the form of virginity. If you do not believe this, learn from Ezekiel: "And he turned me back along the way of the gate of the sanctuary of the outer court, the one facing east, and it was closed. And the Lord said to me: This gate shall remain closed; it shall not be opened, and no one shall pass through it, for the Lord, the God of Israel, shall enter and go out through it, and it shall remain closed" (Ezekiel 44:1-2). "Every male opening the womb shall be called holy to the Lord" (Luke 2:23). But this one is not only holy. As much as he surpasses in sanctification, so much does he also excel in birth and rise above the commandment of the law. Nevertheless, it says, "to offer a sacrifice according to what is said in the law of the Lord, a pair of turtledoves or two young pigeons" (Luke 2:24). Luke left the law incomplete, not seized by ignorance but guided by wisdom. The law said "a lamb and a young pigeon," but if the one offering could not afford it, it commanded "a pair of turtledoves or two young pigeons and fine flour." Luke, however, omitted the offering of the wealthy, for he remembered the poor one who willingly became poor for our sake. He had no lodging, it says; how could he have acquired a lamb? Wrapped in swaddling clothes in a manger, how could he offer a sheep? Rather, he had no need of a lamb, for he himself was "the lamb of God" (John 1:29), the true sheep. He offered himself for the world. For this reason Luke declared what the law commanded, and signified what Christ was accomplishing.

Then next it says: "And behold, there was a man in Jerusalem whose name was Simeon, and this man was righteous and devout, awaiting the consolation of Israel, and the Holy Spirit was upon him. And it had been revealed to him by the Holy Spirit that he would not see death before he had seen the Lord's Christ" (Luke 2:25-26). Great is Simeon's wealth, varied are the commander's weapons, the plant is laden with fruits, the vine is laden with grapes. He was not only "a man," but he was also named Simeon. In addition, he was not only "righteous," but also "devout"; and he sought consolation for Israel; and "the Holy Spirit was upon him"; and he had received a revelation that he would not see death before he had seen the Lord's Christ. "Behold, a man"—where? "In Jerusalem." The word carries astonishment; the phrase is full of wonder. A man in Jerusalem, about which the prophet Zephaniah introduced God himself saying: "I will search Jerusalem with a lamp and will not find a man" (Zephaniah 1:12). Does the light need a lamp? No, he says, but he calls the law a lamp. "And behold, a man in Jerusalem whose name was Simeon." And what is the interpretation of the name that is given? "Hearing of God." So he acquired a name befitting his way of life through the Spirit's dispensation. For where there is "hearing of God," there is certainly obedience to the law, keeping of commandments, the course of a good life, the goal of salvation drawing near to its end. In these things the true man is characterized, about whom these words were fittingly added.

"And this man was righteous and devout, awaiting the consolation of Israel" (Luke 2:25). This is the goal of a righteous man: not to seek his own good, but that of another and of the many, to become a partaker of the common salvation, not of his own enjoyment. "And the Holy Spirit," it says, "was upon him." Simeon was a vehicle of the Lord, a throne of God, and for this reason he received in his hands the King of the ages.
notes: The source text contains several spacing anomalies (e.g., 'ἐζη μίωσε' for 'ἐζημίωσε', 'ἐξω τέρας' for 'ἐξωτέρας', 'κυ ρίῳ' for 'κυρίῳ', 'πα ράκλησιν' for 'παράκλησιν', 'νό μος' for 'νόμος', 'ἄν θρωπος' for 'ἄνθρωπος', 'ἐ κτήσατο' for 'ἐκτήσατο', 'τῆς ἐξω τέρας' for 'τῆς ἐξωτέρας') that appear to be line-break artifacts or OCR damage; the gloss treats them as the intended continuous words.

problems.quote: Luke set forth the law as incomplete
problems.source_quote: Ἀτελῆ τὸν νόμον ὁ Λουκᾶς οὐκ ἀγνοίᾳ κρατηθείς, σοφίᾳ δὲ ὁδηγηθεὶς ἐξέθετο
problems.why: Ἀτελῆ goes with what follows (the abbreviated offering), not 'incomplete law.' Luke presented the law's abbreviated form, not an incomplete law.
problems.fix: Luke presented the abbreviated form of the law, not seized by ignorance but guided by wisdom.

problems.quote: the outer gate of the sanctuary that faces east

problems.why: Source reads ἐξω τέρας (outer court), not 'outer gate'; the gate faces east, not the court.
problems.fix: the gate of the sanctuary of the outer court, the one facing east
problems.ruling: Source has τῆς πύλης τῶν ἁγίων τῆς ἐξωτέρας—'the outer gate of the sanctuary,' not 'outer gate of the sanctuary that faces east'; ἐξωτέρας modifies πύλης, not a separate 'court.'

problems.fix: he received in his hands the King of the ages.
problems.ruling: English omits τὸν βασιλέα τῶν αἰώνων 'the King of the ages'; major Christological title lost from text.

problems.fix: He did not break the seal of nature, nor did he harm the one who bore him

problems.quote: Luke presented the incomplete form of the law
